Tergooi MC | 20 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate

Clinical review prompted by a PSA reading of 8.4 ng/mL and a previously documented PI-RADS 4 abnormality.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic parenchyma occupies 45.02 mL. T2 sequences highlight a 12 mm focal hypointensity situated in the left peripheral zone at the mid-gland. Diffusion-weighted imaging and ADC maps confirm marked restricted diffusion with correspondingly low apparent diffusion coefficients, aligning with a PI-RADS 4 classification. Dynamic contrast enhancement reveals early, focal uptake. Seminal vesicles remain clear. Capsular integrity is intact with no suspicious lymph nodes detected. Bladder and rectal walls are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone mid-prostate.
Prostate volume 45.02 mL; PSA density 0.187 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.7531718.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical follow-up addresses recent prostate developments. A PSA measurement of 8.4 ng/mL marks an increase from the 3.6 ng/mL value recorded in August 2023. In light of the earlier biopsy confirming ISUP GG 2 pathology, the case was forwarded to the urology outpatient department for further assessment.

previous_notes.author: Dr. P. van Dijk (GP)
previous_notes.text: Prostate cancer monitoring update. The most recent PSA reading stands at 3.6 ng/mL, reflecting a decline from the 5.4 ng/mL level noted in February 2022. The individual reports no urological symptoms aside from troublesome lower urinary tract complaints.
